comments.author: @HappyTravel99
comments.text: Thank you so much for watching our video! We wish you all the best. If you enjoyed it, please leave a "1" in the comments to let us know! ❤

comments.author: @Loadedwithflavour
comments.text: I liked your video and have been to most of the places in it, but if you really wanted to highlight places where "civilization ends" you could have mentioned Winter Harbour or Bamfield or Zeballos on Vancouver Island or Atlin or Stewart or Dease Lake or Gingolx on the mainland. You can drive to all of these places and each is a place where people live and work. And I'm sure others will mention equally notable places that I didn't mention.

comments.author: @LifeDocumentary-x7b
comments.text: The lifestyle shown here is completely different from what most people experience every day.

comments.author: @DwelliaTV
comments.text: I love how they turn the wild storms into an experience around [12:16]. Instead of fighting nature, they embrace its raw power!

comments.author: @TravelLives-99
comments.text: I had no idea Canada had a desert with rattlesnakes and temperatures over 110oF! The contrast between the rainy coast and the dry interior is incredible. What a fascinating place!

comments.author: @LatitudesofLife365
comments.text: British Columbia looks like a dream for anyone who loves nature and peaceful living. The breathtaking mountains, endless forests, beautiful lakes, and remote communities make this place truly special. It's amazing how people can enjoy such a quiet lifestyle surrounded by some of the most spectacular scenery in the world.

comments.author: @Thehinterlandlens
comments.text: Some people spend millions escaping the world, while others are lucky enough to call this place home

comments.author: @Artemisia-j2d
comments.text: Hotels in Tofino literally branding torrential winter Pacific storms as a luxury vacation season and lending out free 'Tofino slippers'... genius coastal marketing!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Absolutely! 😄 Only in Tofino could wild winter storms become a luxury experience! There's something magical about watching the powerful Pacific waves from a cozy hotel room. They've truly turned wild weather into something people actually look forward to. Thanks for sharing this wonderful observation!

comments.author: @TheUrbanFacts
comments.text: This was a beautifully crafted look at the incredible diversity of British Columbia! It's fascinating how different the lifestyle can be just a few hours apart. Thank you for sharing these stories

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: Working at a ski resort sounds like a dream until you find out how hard it is to afford a place to live😵‍💫😵‍💫. Anyone here worked in Whistler? Is housing really that difficult?🤔

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: What fascinates me most is how people in remote British Columbia maintain their communities despite the enormous distances and harsh winters. Beautiful scenery is one thing, but the resilience and independence of the people who call these wild places home are what really deserve respect.

comments.author: @manfredwesteroth8241
comments.text: The temp in Osoyoos was at 45 not at 113!!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Thank you for pointing that out! You're totally right — it was 45°C. I used Fahrenheit (113°F) in the video, so it definitely sounds crazy if you're thinking in Celsius!
